detail: Fix #74: a task seal never exceeds LINE_MAX_BYTES (changes capped at build), an over-long valid line stays visible to read-back and redact, and the V1 hint names memory redact

data.goal: Fix #74: a task seal never exceeds LINE_MAX_BYTES (changes capped at build), an over-long valid line stays visible to read-back and redact, and the V1 hint names memory redact

detail: R-a-seal-s-changes-are-emptied-even-when-c-6be5: A seal's changes are emptied even when cutting them cannot make the line fit

data.title: A seal's changes are emptied even when cutting them cannot make the line fit
data.label: KNOWN FACT
data.what: _fit_changes sets changes to [] with both markers when another field (a huge files list) keeps the seal over LINE_MAX_BYTES: the change table is lost and the line is still over (review L1, reproduced with 10 small rows and a 70 KB files list).
data.likelihood: rare: needs a task that names thousands of files explicitly; the totals survive in changes_truncated
data.fix: when the line is still over with changes == [], leave the seal as it was

detail: R-memory-pack-is-blocked-with-a-misleading-eb16: memory pack is blocked with a misleading message while a period holds an over-long entry

data.title: memory pack is blocked with a misleading message while a period holds an over-long entry
data.label: INFERENCE
data.what: An over-long entry is now kept in the packed data, parse_package reports it, and pack raises 'the pack does not hold the batches rid set' after the target file was already written beside the batches (review L2, read from the code, not run).
data.likelihood: only in a repository that still carries an over-long line; safer than before, when the line was silently dropped by pack
data.fix: name the over-long line and 'memory redact' in pack's refusal, checked before the target is written

detail: R-the-seal-size-fix-is-not-pinned-at-its-b-f832: The seal-size fix is not pinned at its boundary, for non-ASCII paths, or on the already-sealed export path

data.title: The seal-size fix is not pinned at its boundary, for non-ASCII paths, or on the already-sealed export path
data.label: RISK
data.what: No test of the exact-fit boundary, the guard loop, multi-byte or escaped paths (checked by hand: correct), the byte-identical V1 fix text of other errors, or the 'already sealed' branch of export in a stuck repository on its own (review L3).
data.likelihood: the code is correct today; a later edit of _fit_changes or check_packages could regress without a red test
data.fix: add the boundary, non-ASCII and already-branch cases to tests/test_memory_compact.py and tests/test_memory_cleanup.py

detail: R-a-deeply-nested-package-line-raises-recu-9ef9: A deeply nested package line raises RecursionError in parse_package instead of a V1 finding

data.title: A deeply nested package line raises RecursionError in parse_package instead of a V1 finding
data.label: RISK
data.what: json.loads of a line nested deeper than about 1000 levels raises RecursionError, which parse_package does not catch: the pre-push validator and every load_packages caller crash. It existed for lines under 64 KB; over-long lines are now parsed too, so the size bound is gone (review I1, out of the task's scope).
data.likelihood: needs a hostile or corrupt package; outside the fixtures
data.fix: catch RecursionError beside ValueError and report 'not JSON'

detail: R-only-a-seal-s-changes-are-cut-to-the-lin-0b97: Only a seal's changes are cut to the line limit: a huge files list or scope entry still gives an over-long line

data.title: Only a seal's changes are cut to the line limit: a huge files list or scope entry still gives an over-long line
data.label: RISK
data.what: A seal over LINE_MAX_BYTES because of files, and a non-seal entry over it (a scope entry whose added list names thousands of paths), are written as they are. They are now visible to read-back and V1 names 'memory redact <rid> --field <largest field>', so the repository is repairable by hand, not automatically; a redacted list field becomes the string '[redacted]'.
data.likelihood: needs a task registered with thousands of explicit paths instead of globs
data.fix: cap the other list fields at build the way changes is capped, with their own totals
